symptom: git push is rejected because the remote has newer commits
steps: Someone pushed to the same branch before you. Run 'git pull --rebase' to bring in their commits first.
If there are conflicts, fix them, run 'git add <file>' and then 'git rebase --continue'.
Do not use 'git push --force' on a shared branch, because it can delete other people's work.

symptom: Merge conflict after git pull or git merge
steps: Run 'git status' to list the files with conflicts.
Open each file and find the lines between <<<<<<< and >>>>>>>.
Keep the lines you want, delete the marker lines and save the file.
Run 'git add <file>' for each fixed file, then 'git commit' to finish the merge.

symptom: Authentication failed when pushing to GitHub
steps: GitHub no longer accepts your account password for git over HTTPS.
Sign in through Git Credential Manager when the browser window opens, or create a personal access token in GitHub under Settings, then Developer settings.
If an old password is saved, remove the github.com entry from Windows Credential Manager (or Keychain Access on a Mac).
Run 'git push' again and sign in through the browser, or paste the token when asked for a password.

symptom: I committed a file by mistake, such as .env
steps: Stop git tracking the file but keep it on your computer with 'git rm --cached <file>'.
Add the file name to .gitignore so it is not added again.
If the file held a password or key, change that secret straight away, because it is still in the git history.

symptom: Git says I am in a "detached HEAD" state
steps: This means you checked out a commit instead of a branch, so new commits will not belong to any branch.
To keep changes you made here, create a branch with 'git switch -c <new-branch-name>'.
To go back to normal, run 'git switch <branch-name>', for example 'git switch develop'.
